title: DeploymentConfig
description:
Nexus config struct for values known only at deployment time.

Note the [`JsonSchema`] derive is just for `test_deployment_config_schema`, which is there to guard us against accidentally changing this struct without giving the proper care and consideration.

We skip adding the Dropshot config fields to the schema because [`ConfigDropshot`] doesn't implement [`JsonSchema`]; this isn't ideal, but we can at least lean on the `dropshot` crate's semver adherance to avoid accidental changes to the underlying config formats for those fields.

Deliberate changes to this struct require careful consideration to avoid breaking anything on update, and existing TOML example/test config files in this repo should also be updated accordingly. Once this has been done, the expected output for `test_deployment_config_schema` can be updated by running the test with `EXPECTORATE=overwrite`.

dropshot_external_additional_addresses.description:
Additional addresses to listen on for the external API.

When set, Nexus launches additional external API servers bound to each of these addresses, reusing all other settings (TLS, request limits, etc.) from `dropshot_external`. This is mainly used to serve the external API on both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

external_dns_servers.description: External DNS servers Nexus can use to resolve external hosts.

external_http_clients.description: Configuration for HTTP clients to external services.

internal_dns.description: Describes how Nexus should find internal DNS servers for bootstrapping.

rack_id.description: Uuid of the Rack where Nexus is executing.

record_db_claim_backtraces.description:
By default, we capture backtraces when claiming a connection from the DB pool, but setting this flag to `false` will disable that behavior.

This flag is intended as an escape hatch in case we ever encounter an unexpected pathological case where capturing backtraces is slow enough to be an issue.

Note that we probably shouldn't need a default here, but I'm leaving it for now just to be safe in case there are any update-related corner cases where this might matter. We can remove this in a future release.

techport_external_server_port.description:
Port on which the "techport external" dropshot server should listen. This dropshot server copies _most_ of its config from `dropshot_external` (so that it matches TLS, etc.), but builds its listening address by combining `dropshot_internal`'s IP address with this port.

We use `serde(default = ...)` to ensure we don't break any serialized configs that were created before this field was added. In production we always expect this port to be constant, but we need to be able to override it when running tests.

ExternalHttpClientConfig.description: Configuration for HTTP clients to external services.

interface.description: If present, bind all TCP connections for external HTTP clients on the specified interface name.

treat_loopback_as_external.description:
Whether external HTTP clients are permitted to make requests to loopback addresses (and names in the special-use "localhost." zone).

External HTTP clients normally refuse to make requests to any address that isn't external to the rack, including loopback addresses. Test environments, however, run their "external" servers on localhost, so the test suite needs a way to turn that off.

InternalDns.description: The mechanism Nexus should use to contact the internal DNS servers.

This is a more common usage for production.

This is less desirable in production, but can give value in test scenarios.

Ipv6Net.title: An IPv6 subnet
Ipv6Net.description: An IPv6 subnet, including prefix and subnet mask

Ipv6Subnet.description: Wraps an [`Ipv6Net`] with a compile-time prefix length.

TreatLoopbackAsExternal.description:
Whether HTTP clients for external services permit requests to loopback addresses.

This is an enum rather than a `bool`, so that if you want to turn on the test-only config, you have to type the string "yes_for_test_purposes_only" in the config file so you know what you're doing.

oneOf.description: Loopback addresses are considered "external". This must only be used in test environments.
